notes.title: Missions and Monsters DLC - The Wrangler
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Today, we're going over the last of the new human classes that will be introduced in [i]Missions and Monsters[/i]: the [b]Wrangler [/b]class.

As we've mentioned before, the [b]Wrangler [/b]class will be pivotal to the growth of your [i]Beastmaster [/i]units, because of its [i]Tame [/i]ability that lets you recruit monsters during battle. But, the [b]Wrangler [/b]class is a lot more than just a supporting actor to your [i]Beastmasters [/i]and brings many powerful abilities of its own.

The [b]Wrangler [/b]focuses heavily on interacting with monsters in general, be they allies or enemies, so it tends to lend itself better to a supporting role. Without any monsters on the field on either side, the [b]Wrangler [/b]is probably not going to outshine most other classes. But with monsters around... it's a different story. And with monsters stronger than ever in [i]Missions and Monsters[/i], you'll quickly find yourself welcoming the [b]Wrangler[/b]'s expertise!

[h1]Abilities:[/h1]
Let's go over their abilities, passives, and counter:

[b]Counter[/b]: 
[b]Might[/b]: Counters any offensive action taken on the character by using Atk and Mnd up. This gives the Wrangler an easy means to pack a bigger punch if they'd rather be more hands-on than supportive.

[b]Passives[/b]:
[b]Skirmish[/b]: The character will be able to move 1 extra tile at the end of their turn. So if the unit moves before it attacks, it will get a second movement phase of 1 tile after its attack, and if it moves after it attacks, it will get to move 1 extra tile. This gives the Wrangler extra mobility and versatility, and even allows for extra back-attacks by melee units.

[b]Owner's Pride[/b]: Whenever an allied monster unit falls in battle or defeats an enemy, the Wrangler gets a stacking 10% bonus to their speed stat (up to 40%), allowing them to snowball their advantage or come back from a tough situation more easily.

[b]Actives[/b]:
[b]Tag Team[/b]: The Wrangler can select an ally monster unit in range and "swap them out" for a benched monster unit. The new unit will get all the buffs, debuffs, current HP/MP and turn completion transferred to them. This grants the Wrangler immense versatility as they can change the party composition itself as the battle progresses.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/80999c57ed7c6db5e8cc4adde6147f2a63a07dc1.gif[/img]

[b]Tame[/b]: This lets the Wrangler recruit enemy monsters. The chance is based on the enemy's current HP (the lower, the better) and won't work on bosses and special enemies. But there are otherwise no restrictions.

[b]Attack![/b]: The Wrangler orders all allied monsters on the map to attack the first target in range directly in front of them. With careful planning and placement, this ability has the potential to be devastating.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/519983f8f7b4bb09127ec1fc6fb0208b7f8ef91f.gif[/img]

[b]Frenzy![/b]: This gives Atk Up to all allied monsters, but removes Mnd Up from all of them. 
[b]Calm...[/b]: This gives Mnd Up to all allied monsters, but removes Atk Up from all of them. A quick way to bolster all of your allied monster friends.

[b]Heel![/b]: This allows the Wrangler to select an enemy or allied monster within 5 tiles and teleport them to a tile adjacent to the Wrangler. This gives the Wrangler great control over the placement of all monsters on the field and can be used both offensively and defensively to great effect.

[b]Beast Whisperer[/b]: Allows the Wrangler to use Mind Control on an enemy monster (Mind Control is a superior form of Charm where the target will get an immediate turn, controlled by the Wrangler, on top of being left with the Charm status afterwards). This ability is melee range, so it's a little riskier than other Wrangler abilities, but very potent.

[b]Quicken Monster[/b]: A version of Quicken that targets only Monsters. It costs less MP as a trade-off.

[b]Hunt[/b]: An attack that deals high damage to monster units, but poor damage to humans and bzils. Counts as a regular attack.


And that's it for all of the [b]Wrangler[/b]'s abilities! Their kit is unique and a little more subtle to use than most other classes, but if the field has many monsters and you're clever about placement, their potential is immense, both defensively and offensively.


Stay safe everyone! And thanks for your continued support.

notes.title: Missions and Monsters DLC - The Beastmaster
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

This week, we're going to cover in detail one of the new classes that will be available in [i]Missions and Monsters[/i]: the [b]Beastmaster [/b]class!

The [b]Beastmaster [/b]is our biggest class yet, with a ton of abilities. They are somewhat of an hybrid between a regular class and the [i]Gadgeteer [/i]class, but with many new and unique mechanics.

The [i]Gadgeteer [/i]style part of the class comes from the way they will learn 14 of their abilities. These abilities are each tied to a specific pet monster and have 2 parts: the active part, which works the same way as any regular ability: you select the ability, you choose the target(s) and then you use it. Those have a wide range of effects, as the [b]Beastmaster [/b]is incredibly versatile: damage, healing, debuffs, buffs, special abilities...

Once the ability is used, the pet that it's associated with will appear next to the caster and remain there (almost) indefinitely. You can have up to 3 pets out at once per character, and if you summon a 4th one, the oldest pet will go away. Each character can only have 1 of each pet out, meaning they must have 3 different pets out at once. This is per character, so having 2 Beastmasters out won't interfere with their pets' availability.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/3afa33cb738b1965cd78cf36b52e0d905c65ff10.gif[/img]

At the end of the character's turn, any pet they have out will apply their effect to targets adjacent to the character. All pets are "smart", so healing pets will only apply their "end of turn effect" to friendlies and damaging pets will only target enemies, etc.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/b2599bac02305b1637809e2e2da99712a1f702c0.gif[/img]
In the example above, 3 pets are out: the [i]Blardger Brat[/i], which deals damage, the [i]Daodrenner Kit[/i], which heals allies and the [i]Arpia Guttersnipe[/i], which has a chance to poison (and refresh poison duration on) adjacent enemies. All the effects happen at once so the information is displayed as quickly as possible.

These 14 pets are unlocked by recruiting the corresponding monster, which means that once a monster is recruited, every Arbiter on your team will have access to the given pet summon (assuming they have access to the [b]Beastmaster [/b]class to begin with). In this way, those behave much like gadgets. Monsters can be recruited through missions or through Taming (with the new [i]Wrangler [/i]class). 

On top of these 14 pets that can be summoned, the [b]Beastmaster [/b]has access to 7 more abilities that are learned normally through their skill tree (so those are not shared across all units and must be learned individually, like regular class skills).

Those abilities are "[b]Pet Dismisses[/b]" and are a new mechanic to the game. 
The Dismissal abilities can only be used when the character has at least 1 pet out. When they use a Dismiss ability, all their currently deployed pets will be dismissed and the spell will gain more power for each pet dismissed that way. The dismissal abilities have a very wide range of utility (and scale well with a high number of pets), such as damaging enemies, healing an allly or even all allies at once, revives, character displacement, etc.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/a926a03262eb082254b81fab27e4a177f0a3d0a9.gif[/img]

All in all, the [b]Beastmaster [/b]is a VERY versatile class, with varied play styles possible. The player can opt to maximize the pets' "end of turn" effects and run around with an aura of healing/damage to everything in range, or they can opt to focus on the Dismiss abilities, bringing out pets as fast as possible to prime big ratios to Dismiss abilities. Or they can pursue a balanced approach of the above, of course.

One thing is certain, the true power of the class is tied to the cute pets it can bring out. And to help with that, there are various abilities to summon them faster, such as the counter [b]Loyal Friends[/b], which will trigger on any offensive action taken on the caster by summoning a random pet, thus helping the character bring out 3 pets faster than normal.

The [b]Beastmaster [/b]has 2 powerful passives, one which restores MP for each buff/debuff/pet that wears off or is dismissed/dispelled from the character, helping them build MP faster as they use their pets (or through buffs/debuffs removal).

Their second passive is called [b]Rampart[/b], and it creates a "zone of control" around the unit, preventing any enemies from moving further once they move to an "adjacent tile" to the character. They'll only be able to walk past that tile on the next turn.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/b9ef9e431874b40b9226cc88798c2dd50cf68400.png[/img]
Here, Reiner can't walk past the unit with [b]Rampart[/b], as the shortest path is blocked by Rampart and he doesn't have enough movement to go fully around.

With all these tools at their disposal, we expect the [b]Beastmaster [/b]will quickly become a fan favorite!

[b]Let us know what you think![/b] And as always, thanks for the support!


Lastly, we hope everyone stays safe during these difficult times >.<

notes.title: Missions and Monsters DLC - Monster Variants In-Depth
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Today, we'll go into the details of the [b]Monster Variants [/b]system that we briefly covered a few weeks ago.

[h1]Quick Recap:[/h1]
In [i]Missions and Monsters[/i], the player will be able to recruit monster units, either from [b]Taming [/b]them (with the new [i]Wrangler [/i]class), or by earning them as rewards from various [i]Missions[/i].

Monsters behave a little differently than humans: they can't change their "monster class", such as being a [i]Vangal[/i], an [i]Ercinee [/i]or a [i]Daodrenner[/i]. Instead, they have access to mini-classes called [b]Variants[/b]. Each monster can use 2 such variants on top of their basic monster class (for a total of 3 classes equipped).
They can set up a [b]primary Variant[/b] and a [b]secondary Variant[/b]. It's easy to think of them as a main class and a sub class for the most part. Monsters gain access to the active ability sets from their equipped variants on top of their monster ability set and they'll automatically use any known passives tied to the variants they're using, thus equipping up to 6 passives in total.

Thus, monsters gain access to more passives at a time, but have a little less flexibility when picking them. They also gain access to more sets of abilities (3 rather than 2), but those sets have fewer abilities than human sets would have. All in all, they have their own strengths and weaknesses and should prove to be quite an interesting addition to a player's arsenal.

[h1]In-depth overview:[/h1]
Monsters need to use AP to unlock abilities from their class and variants, just like humans. Since a monster's base class can't be changed ever, learning everything on it is somewhat quick, so we're keeping things simple and awarding AP to both their [b]monster class[/b] and their [b]primary variant[/b] at the same time. 
It's also worth noting that when taming a monster, they will come knowing all the skills they knew when you tamed them, meaning quite often their monster class will start almost maxed (or fully maxed if recruiting a Tier 3 monster), so the real use of AP lies in the [b]Variants[/b].

New Variants can be learned in many different ways: through missions, by using special badges, and by learning enough abilities from other Variants (so, all in all, a similar way to humans). Variants (and base monster classes) will work with the Vicarious AP system to help the player train all their monstrous forces.

When it comes to stats, monsters have fixed stats that depend on their monster class (and tier). Thus, their stats will always be the same for 2 monsters of the same type (assuming they are currently using the same primary variant, more on that in a bit). All monsters in [i]Fell Seal[/i] have 3 different tiers (such as [i]Vangal[/i], [i]Komainu [/i]and [i]Gyaum[/i]), and each tier confers higher stats and sometimes improved resistances and such.
A monster's skill tree has 2 [b]"Tier Up" nodes [/b]that can be purchased and will increase the monster's tier, resulting in higher stats, etc:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/91d6f413b87547b7c39e9382742e2ab721c3989f.png[/img]


The [b]Primary Variant [/b]is more or less treated like a human's main class. The monster will gain AP for that Variant. The 2nd Variant behaves like a sub class, meaning the monster won't be gaining AP for it, but will gain access to its active abilities, and passives.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/5b625887d76a9d05a462c0413f4b6bc705d4e8ff.png[/img]

The primary Variant isn't just about gaining AP though, as it also influences the monster's stats. The primary Variant has an effect on the monster's base stats, immunities, elemental resistances, movement, jump, flight, swimming, etc.

For example, using [i]Fire Drake[/i] as a primary variant will grant a %-based bonus to atk, mnd, def, res, a bonus to Fire and earth resistances, and a malus to water resistance. The Aerial variant grants Flying, a small evasion boost, earth resistance, and weakness to thunder, etc.

Each variant has different modifications; some are pretty small and others a little bigger, depending on various factors.

The primary variant can be selected from the [b]Class wheel [/b]and will show the resulting stats and the bonuses granted, showing exactly how the primary variant will change things (that screen isn't finished, so we don't have a screenshot ready quite yet!)


[h1]Visuals:[/h1]
As usual, we're all about giving the player options, so we're adding visual customization to the monsters. By default, recruited monsters have "automated" visuals that will show specific "accessories" representing their 2 equipped variants and show the base monster sprite representing their monster tier. This is how enemy monsters behave.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/6b30df915bf4d5872b929d1e5b352b2eb53494fc.gif[/img]
[i](Mystic/Clockwork Kawa)[/i]

Using the character customization screen, the player can select a color for the monster from the 3 tier sprites the monster has, rather than using the color of their current tier. They can also opt to select any number of variant accessories to create their monster's look, rather than use those tied to their equipped variants.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/ce29b344ddbcd88d40e05b58e83008ad60890048.png[/img]

There's a lot to talk about when it comes to [b]monster variants[/b], but hopefully we haven't forgotten anything! Let us know if you have any questions or comments, and thanks again for the support!

notes.title: Missions and Monsters DLC - Hunts
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

[i]Missions and Monsters[/i] is a collection of new systems, updates and additions to the game, resulting in a richer and more engaging gameplay experience. One of these new additions is the special [b]Hunts[/b].

[h1]Hunts:[/h1]
The [b]Hunts[/b] tie together the new [i]missions [/i]system and the new [i]monsters variants [/i]system (a quick refresher on this can be [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/699170/announcements/detail/3453632564279136594]found right here[/url]). For most hunts, you'll unlock them by undertaking a special mission, or a "mission chain", which is multiple missions that must be completed in order and culminate into a difficult and rewarding special mission. These missions will become available from around the mid-game, right up to the final fight in the game. 
After the mission is completed, it'll open a new "[b]Hunt event[/b]", which will show a special icon on the world map, much in the same way as [i]character events [/i].
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/990083cf5c7c45c74a7525571356a274e0fb8629.png[/img]

The player can then visit that node and trigger the [b]Hunt event[/b], which will feature a custom battle against a very powerful hand-crafted named monster unit, boasting a complex monster variants setup. Achieving victory in a [b]Hunt [/b]should be a challenging endeavor and will award the player unique rewards. Each Hunt can only be completed once.

[h1]New Maps:[/h1]
On top of the new systems, new classes and new abilities, we'll be adding new maps as well. Notably, both [b]Port Grendel [/b]and [b]Fenfjord [/b]will get a town map, replete with special encounters and patrols. But we'll be adding many other extra maps as well (you can expect many [b]Hunts [/b]to take place on these new maps we'll be adding!)

notes.title: Missions and Monsters DLC - Monsters
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Today, we'll be covering our plans for the [b]monsters[/b]! We'll be focusing on the monsters themselves, as well as their new sub-classes, which are tentatively called  [b]monster variants[/b].

The short and simple version is that monsters have their base class (Vangal, for example) and then can equip up to [b]2 variants[/b]. They'll get access to the ability set of the variant, as well as their passives, on top of their base monster class. We're still tuning, but the current idea is that each variant has 2 active abilities, 2 passives and 1 counter. One of the goals is to give them something different than humans in the form of more equipped passives, while expanding their base abilities without crowding them too much.

We're focusing on the monsters today, but the systems in [i]Missions and Monsters [/i]are all intricately tied together, so many of the features tied to monsters and variants will be obtained through special missions and new classes. We'll have updates about those later!


[h1]Monsters Specifics:[/h1]
[i]Missions and Monsters[/i] will be making monsters recruitable, so they can now join your Arbiter forces. You'll have to recruit them in a different manner than regular units, though. Monsters will join the player as rewards from special Missions or from being tamed during combat by the new [b]Wrangler[/b] class (which we'll cover in a later update). Each monster base class (such as Vangal, Ercinee, etc.) will have its own skill tree, with their upgraded tiers (eg. Vangal -> Komainu -> Gyaum) being a node on their tree they can spend AP on to learn. There will be a tutorial on the process added early in the game to make sure things are well explained!

The monster variants can be seen as classes that the monsters can learn, and they function in a similar fashion to the human classes. A monster [b]cannot change its base class [/b], but they can [b]equip up to 2 variant classes [/b]and [b]1 counter[/b]. A monster unit will be able to set its 2 variants and its counter from the UI, which means that all its passives come directly from its base class and 2 variants. They get 6 passives in total, but they have a little less flexibility than humans in selecting them.

The variant classes will have their [b]own skill tree and AP pool[/b] and will unlock their abilities and passives in the usual way. New variants will be unlocked in a variety of ways, including having a high enough level in other variants, mission rewards, and special monster badges.

On the visual side of things, each variant will have its own unique sprite representation (like human classes have their hats) so it'll be obvious at a glance which variants a monster is sporting. Since each monster can have up to 2 variants equipped, they could be showing 2 different sprites at once.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/88d62eb42b30894bc9984ce3ae472e68192c8325.gif[/img]
[i]Here, a Thorned Vangal uses Thornstrike on a Venomous Skeletal Daodrenner.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/60d28a74423eacfd82f0ffdb2199c723db88c21b.gif[/img]
[i]Here, we can see a Blardger showing many of its possible variants, although only 1 at a time (there could be up to 2 shown at once).[/i]

[h1]Closing Words:[/h1]
One of the reasons we didn't have recruitable monsters in [i]Fell Seal[/i] before now is that we wanted to make sure they would be interesting and customizable enough compared to human classes. We feel that too many games in the genre have recruitable monsters tossed in, but never bother to make them as attractive when compared to human classes, which tend to be more feature-rich. With our system, we're aiming to change that and make monsters both viable and interesting. They'll have different pros and cons than humans, but ultimately should balance out well when compared. It'll be up to player preference at that point!

[b]Thanks to everyone for the continued support![/b]

notes.title: Missions and Monsters DLC - Splash Art
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

notes.title: Missions and Monsters #3 - Samurai Class
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

This week, we want to cover one of the new classes that we're adding in [i]Missions and Monsters[/i], the
[b]Samurai[/b] class!

But before that, some quick notes about Missions:

Since posting our devlog on the Missions system, we've been thinking about adding a currency cost to missions. As we've been creating the list of them (we're up to 79 missions so far!), it became obvious the cost was a good idea.

We've decided to use both [b]GP [/b]and [b]CP [/b](Company Points) for the cost. A mission will only have a GP or CP cost at once, but they'll always have a cost. This will help make GP less "trivial" to accrue and give it increased worth. And it will give CP another use apart from being used for [i]Guild Upgrades[/i], which will create an opportunity-cost for them.

This change ties things together neatly and elegantly! It's just a question of creating all the remaining Missions now!

[b]Thanks to everyone that sent us feedback on this, we appreciate it![/b]

[h1]Samurai Class:[/h1]
With [i]Missions and Monsters[/i], we'll be adding [b]3 new base classes [/b]to human units. Base class means they'll be [b]usable by any unit [/b](story and generic) and won't require a badge to open up.
The new classes are tied to missions though, and will only become visible after the associated mission has been completed, on top of having the usual class requirements (eg. 3 Mercenary, 4 Scoundrel, etc.).

The default portrait for the [b]Samurai [/b]unit:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/9d66f52f9b17918e643222c58180bbd9e389249a.png[/img]

The basic design idea behind the [b]Samurai [/b]class is a mix of high-risk/high-reward abilities and passives, as well as a fairly versatile kit. They sport some interesting unique abilities to give them varied options.
[b]Samurais [/b]should be somewhat fragile in the face of taking damage, but deal fairly well with status effects, while providing high damage and utility for the team.

Here's their ability list (please note the names aren't final at this point). As a note, a fair amount of these abilities apply their status effect on the [b]Samurai [/b]themselves, so pay close attention to the wording!

[b]Actives:[/b]
[list][*][b]Overreach:[/b] 8MP. Attack range tied to weapon. Count as a regular attack. Deals 1.2x damage and inflicts def-down on the user.

[*][b]Meditate:[/b] 6MP. Self spell that removes all debuffs and heals 0.6x (mnd) for each debuff removed. Sets user evasion to 0% until next turn.

[*][b]Finisher:[/b] 20MP. Attack range tied to weapon. Count as a regular attack. Deals 2.4x damage and inflicts atk-down on the user.

[*][b]Single Out:[/b] 8MP. Range 5, single target. Inflicts def-down, res-down on the target and force them to turn towards the user.

[*][b]Spirit Sword:[/b] 14MP. Range 1. Does 2.6x (MND) non-elemental damage to the target and inflicts mnd-down on the user.

[*][b]Martial Spirit:[/b] 10MP. A small cross shape centered on the user. It deals 0.35x damage to all units around, inflicts cripple on them and forces them to face the user.

[*][b]Blood Spirit:[/b] 8MP. Range 1. Does 0.6x damage to the target and ignores their def stat. Also inflicts bleed on the user.
[/list]

[b]Passives:[/b]
[list][*][b]Razor Wind:[/b] Can use with any single-target skill. Adds 6MP to the cost and changes the range to 3. Sets user evasion to 0% until the next turn. (This adds a new command, much like Double Cast).

[*][b]Unbreakable Spirit:[/b] Being afflicted by def-down/mnd-down increases atk/mnd by the same amount. Being afflicted by atk-down/mnd-down increases def/res by the same amount.
[/list]

[b]Counter:[/b]
[list][b]Counter Critical: Focus:[/b] Automatically uses Defend and Focus when HP becomes critical.
[/list]

[b]Weapons:[/b] Sword
[b]Armors:[/b] Light, Heavy

[h1]Preview:[/h1]
Here's some of the art we're preparing for the new abilities:

notes.title: DLC Devlog #2 - Guild Upgrades
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!
 
In this week's devlog, we'll detail another system tied to the missions: the [b]Guild Upgrades[/b] system.
 
[h1]Upgrades[/h1]
As mentioned in the previous devlog, the world is divided into 5 different regions. Upgrades can be built into any of these 5 regions and will confer a variety of bonuses, primarily to that region.
 
After selecting the Upgrades section in the Guild, the player can decide in which region they want to build upgrades for. Selecting a region will show it on the world map, show which battle maps are tied to it and which upgrades are currently built on there.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/cb6606389c19ec461f679fea225d94d6c154cb5c.jpg[/img]

Afterwards, the player can build upgrades for the region, or reset current upgrades for the region.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/86b837824b6a3b1ca135481748001d9e96e9c07c.jpg[/img]

Resetting the upgrades will refund a portion of their cost and clear all upgrades from the area, so the player can change their layout if they feel like it. On that screen, the player can see the layout for the selected region and the currently built upgrades if there are any. Each region has its own layout for adding buildings. This example has a 3x4 area to add buildings. Other regions will have different areas, such as a 3x3 or perhaps a 2x3 and a 1x3, etc.
 
Selecting to build a new upgrade will show the list of all possible upgrades the player could create as well as their cost in CP (Company Points). There will be a core of buildings that will be the same for all regions, but some regions will have unique buildings that confer special bonuses or bonuses that pertain to the specific zone better (things tied to poisonous maps for example).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/8487ab7c9374a142ad8e052ff0b958b26e4c4aa4.jpg[/img]

You can see the bonus for the selected upgrade in its description. These bonuses are divided into 3 general categories:
[list][*]Mission Bonuses: these bonuses apply to Mission that are in the same zone as the Upgrade.
[*]Patrol Bonuses: these bonuses apply to Patrols that are in maps that are part of the same zone as the Upgrade.
[*]Global Bonuses: these bonuses apply all the time to all zones. Those are considerably rarer.
[/list]
 
On top of this base bonus that a building confers, there's a concept of [b]synergy[/b], where a building can bolster another building if they happen to be touching on the building grid. For example, the [i]Cantina [/i]will confer a bonus to the [i]Gardens[/i], the [i]Bounty Board [/i]and the [i]Watchtower [/i]if they are built side by side. Thus, the grid available in a region (3x3 vs 2x3 for example) will impact what kind of bonuses you could get in that region. And, of course, the player's choices in placing the buildings will also have an impact on that front.
 
Here's what it looks like when selecting the [i]Gardens[/i], which receives a bonus from the [i]Cantina[/i]. It shows what the bonus would be on that building if it was next to a [i]Cantina[/i], in this case "[i]receive 2x as many components from Gathering[/i]".
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/d42e5ed2a5ea496ae938f7ea054aa17d44c21656.jpg[/img]

Finally, when selecting a specific upgrade, you will be able to place it where you want in the building grid, assuming you have the CP and the grid position isn't already occupied by another building. As you select a position, the "border bonuses" that will be active will light up to show which would be active from placing the building there and greyed out if they wouldn't currently confer a bonus.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/da7ecaf46fd44eb9e2df9f44d1c149d8ad2f0f66.jpg[/img]

The current building icons were taken from some of our maps and aren't final, but they showcase the visual style we're going for with the buildings.
 
[h1]Upgrades Bonuses[/h1]
Currently, there are [b]24 different building [/b]upgrades and each will have its own [b]unique building sprite[/b]. Each has their own bonus and many will have synergy bonuses as well. Here are some examples of the bonuses the upgrades will grant:

[b]Missions:[/b]
[list][*]Missions take 20% less time to complete.
[*]Missions award 20% more CP.
[*]Missions award 2x as many components as normal.
[*]One extra unit can be sent on each mission.
[*]Missions award 20% more AP
[*]…
[/list]
 
[b]Patrols:[/b]
[list][*]While patrolling the region, increase the chance of meeting stray Kawa Bandits 5%
[*]While patrolling the region, increase the chance of meeting stray Zotzits 5%
[*]While patrolling the region, increase damage dealt by player units by 5%.
[*]While patrolling the region, all deployed units will start with Renew.
[*]...
[/list]
 
[b]Global:[/b]
[list][*]Store prices in any store are 5% cheaper when buying.
[*]Guild prices in any guild are 5% cheaper for all services costing GP.
[*]Can run 1 more mission at the same time.
[*]...
[/list]
 
When combined with the [b]Missions[/b], the[b] Guild Upgrades[/b] system should give the player a lot to do outside of battles and help them open up new challenges, areas and rewards.
 
Feel free to send us comments, ideas, feedback and suggestions!
 
[b]Thanks for reading![/b]

notes.title: DLC Devlog #1 - Missions System
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!
  
We've been quite busy hammering the designs down for [b]Missions and Monsters[/b], and we've finally reached a point where we feel we have enough details to start our devlog on the creation process.
 
With each devlog, we'll be focusing on one of the new systems that [b]Missions and Monsters[/b] will be adding to [i]Fell Seal[/i]. This week, that's [b]missions[/b]! But first, a quick refresher on the general scope of the DLC.
 

[h1]General Concept[/h1]
[b]Missions and Monsters[/b] isn't meant as a continuation of [i]Fell Seal[/i]'s story, but rather to extend and add to the core systems of the game, as well as add new challenges and content.
 
As such, the plan is to add a [b]missions [/b]system, a [b]guild upgrade[/b] system, [b]recruitable monsters[/b], a [b]monster-taming[/b] system, [b]monster classes[/b], [b]new encounters[/b], [b]new classes [/b]and [b]new crafting recipes[/b]. We're also adding [b]large encounters [/b]that will feature a lot more combatants on each side, for putting to work more of those units you've been collecting.
 

[h1]Missions[/h1]
The new [b]missions [/b]system is wide-reaching and meant to achieve several goals.
It will give more things to do for "benched units", with some missions giving special rewards, opening new content and being a viable method to procure many crafting components. Missions can also serve as an alternative means of earning EXP and AP for benched units, although in that case they tend to yield less impressive loot. Most missions will be repeatable, but some will be unique and award something quite special.
 
It'll be up to the player to decide which style of missions they want to focus on, as they can only run a limited amount of missions at once.
 
[b]Missions [/b](and [b]guild upgrades[/b], which we'll cover in a later devlog) are accessed through the [b]Guild menu[/b]:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/fe8dcff709a8de9542a4a2a51aec2aee867793d9.jpg[/img]
A new resource called [b]Company Points [/b](CP) will be added next to the current GP bar. Currently, CPs are only used to purchase Guild Upgrades, but we're considering adding a cost in CP to run Missions as well.
 
Once you've selected Missions from the Guild, you need to select the [b]Region [/b]in which you want to start a mission. There are [b]5 Regions[/b] in the game and they open up as you unlock new nodes on the world map.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/64e4c8f66b7fc98fe59cf6a7ea23984b1f8e54b5.jpg[/img]
In this screenshot, only the "Centina Hinterlands" region is available and it's still missing 3 nodes to be fully unlocked. All missions have a location node where they take place, and thus won't be available until the given node has been explored by the player on the world map.
 
After selecting the region, the player can start a mission in that region.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/fc64212976381b49e05ff2a0ba2b29aa2897d8f3.jpg[/img]
Missions that aren't known yet (because they are locked behind a map node, or because they require a previous mission to be completed, for example) are shown as ??? in the list.
 
Missions can be in various states: new, in-progress, completed-and-done, completed-and-redoable. They have a different icon depending on their current state. In the example list, they are all "new" or unknown.
 
Here you can see the rewards of the mission as well as the required participants and how long they last (more info on that later!).
 
Selecting a valid mission will bring the player to a selection screen to decide which units to send on the mission. Only the units participating in the mission will earn the various rewards, such as AP, EXP, etc.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/f45c6ff9f8e00675c63a94098bd02439a2eeb290.jpg[/img]
[b]Story-characters can't be sent on missions[/b] and [b]only recruits[/b] without an injury can be sent. When a unit is sent on a mission, they won't be available to be deployed in a regular battle map.
 
Each mission has a minimum and a maximum of participants and the first participant chosen becomes the [b]leader of the mission[/b]. Once enough units are selected, the mission can be started.
 
Once the mission is started, it'll show as "in-progress" in the missions list.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/7d9646a06b77b61779dc9a9ba37ffb48e80c8f16.jpg[/img]
In-progress missions have their own icon and are always sorted at the end of the list for a quick visual identification. Selecting a mission already in progress will allow the player to cancel it if they want to. Cancelling the mission will free up the units that were running it, but no rewards shall be given for the mission.
 
Currently, the maximum amount of missions that can be run at once is 3, although there is a way to increase that amount via the Guild Upgrades system.
 
When a mission is in progress, it will take some amount of time to complete, usually 30 mins, although that's something we're still tinkering with. After 30 mins of "real life time" has passed, the mission will be completed and display a result for the endeavor anywhere on the world map.
 
[b]Mission success is not guaranteed[/b], although the success rate will be tuned to be pretty high in general. There are multiple ways to increase that, including Guild Upgrades and [b]carefully selecting the leader of the mission[/b]. The class of the leader will grant them a bonus success rate based on the mission. The description of the mission itself will have clues hinting at which type of class would do well on it. This bonus is only applied to the leader of the mission, to reduce the amount of micro-managing of classes that the player has to do for missions, while still providing some incentive for "thinking about it" rather than just clicking through things. Missions can also have a [b]critical success result[/b], in which case bonus rewards will be granted to the player.
 
The overall goal of the missions and guild upgrade systems is to [b]create another layer of interesting actions the player can take "outside of combat"[/b], with a wide array of goals possible, such as farming AP, EXP, GP or CP, as well as focusing on crafting materials, special rewards or unlocking new content.
 
It'll be tied to the [b]Guild Upgrade [/b]system, which we should cover in our next devlog.
 
Feel free to send us comments, ideas, feedback and suggestions about the design or the devlog itself!
 
[b]Thanks everyone![/b]

notes.title: Build 1.1.2
notes.notes:
[h1]Build 1.1.2[/h1]
Hello everyone!

We have a quick update today. Nothing fancy, mostly some minor bug fixes and adding a forgotten portrait.

Here are the full notes:

[u]11/16/2019 - Version 1.1.2[/u]
[h1]UI:[/h1][list][*][b]New Portrait:[/b] Adding a forgotten male portrait.
[*][b]Accessibility:[/b] Adding a new key to help with accessibility for users. The key can be setup in GameConfig.txt file under [UI] by adding "accessibilitymouse=2", which uses the "mouse middle button". Pressing the key in combat will "lock/unlock" the screen so that the cursor doesn't move the map cursor anymore. This allow the player to easily click the "bottom right hints" with the mouse at all times, without changing where the map cursor is on screen. This helps players to navigate the game using exclusively the mouse, without having to rely on the keyboard at all. This key should be moved to the regular key-rebind menu once it's been tested a little more.
[/list]

[h1]Misc:[/h1][list][*][b]Save Files:[/b] Tiny optimizations to the format to make it just a bit smaller.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes:[/h1][list][*][b]Menu Sorting:[/b] Sorting could be used in combat under specific circumstances. Disabling that (sorting units while in combat creates issues with deployment).
[*][b]Hallowed Mind:[/b] Used to incorrectly trigger when being revived by Reraise. Fixed.
[*][b]Class Wheel:[/b] When using the custom option to show monsters sprites to represent Bzil classes in the class changing menu, it was showing human sprites after the last update. Fixed.
[*][b]NG Plus:[/b] When using "Keep AP" with a Newgame  , a certain story character would not correctly retain their AP. Fixed.
[*][b]Mercer Warning:[/b] The warning to let the player know when the optional event with routing certain bandits would become unavailable would show even if the event was already completed. Fixed.
[*][b]Aries Ram:[/b] Last update broke the visuals. Fixed.
[/list]

[h1]Balance:[/h1][list][*][b]Massive Hit:[/b] Increasing MP cost to 16 (from 12).
[/list]

[h1]Modding:[/h1][list][*][b]Monsters:[/b] Adding Monsters.xml file, that allows the player to create new "base monsters entries", which are the building blocks of monsters (it contains their image, portrait, base elemental and status resistances, weapon range, etc). Using this file, monsters can be modified or new monster tiers, or different monsters can be created.
[*][b]GameOptions and Jobs[/b] Deprecating the Hats and Outfits section in the GameOptions.txt to set up the hat and outfit of classes. The class itself will now contain that information in Jobs.xml.
[/list]

notes.title: Build 1.1.1 Keyboard QoL Update!
notes.notes:
[h1]New Hotkeys System:[/h1]
Hello everyone!

Build 1.1.1 is a PC only update with one main goal: improving the mouse keyboard experience by adding hotkeys to all main "commands list".
This will allow players to easily make selections with the keyboard alone without needing to move the mouse and help speed things up. Here's what the menus now look like when using mouse and keyboard:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/e7ea2a9dbce372127613c52385bbc7db98e6c0b4.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/34f569108258500d2ff4dcc0cb21d8becfebaade.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/8eaa4a2ba4b7e921357369b7602bbd2e7c003655.png[/img]

The short version is that you can press these hotkeys to automatically activate them and that things will remain consistent even as you learn new spells and abilities or use different characters. 


[h1]The Details:[/h1]
The numbers on the side are the default keys assigned to "Hotkey 1 to 12" and can be configured in the regular "key binding" menu to be any key.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/895ae6c59e7947278e29916d2fe5ad4520d5fa75.png[/img]

Each action in a list is bound to a specific hotkey, so that they remain consistent through time.
For example, the "End" command in battle will always be mapped to "Hotkey 6", regardless of which other commands are available.
That way, units with Double Cast, Focused Rage, next to a treasure chest, etc., will still use "Hotkey 6" to quickly end their turn so it remains consistent at all times.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/b93ff0a125b61cbade336ea999feef4d07eae832.png[/img]

The concept is the same for skills and spells, where a specific spell, such as "Water II" for example, will always have the same hotkey assigned to it regardless of which spells a Wizard has learned. So, learning "Fire II" later won't suddenly change the hotkey for "Water II" because now there's a new spell before it in the list.
For example, "Sniper Shot" will always be "hotkey 7" on every character at all times, even if you made a beeline for it and skipped most other skills in the Ranger tree.

The only exception to this is when using Double Cast, Infused Edge, etc. The generated list of available spells will simply use the hotkeys in order, since it's not possible to retain "always the same hotkey" across two different groups of abilities, since they would share hotkeys.

Lastly, please note that when using a gamepad, those hotkeys won't be visible in the lists and nothing is changed from the previous state of things.

Let us know how it goes!

notes.title: Build 1.1.0, with New Game Plus!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

[h1]New Build:[/h1]
We released [b]Build 1.1.0[/b] today.
The main addition is a versatile [b]New Game Plus[/b] mode. In keeping true to our style of granting the player as many options as possible, you get to choice what carries over or not to the next game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/6664a63922854ffcd43c07a9422c33ea7b7a74dc.jpg[/img]

The options will be available from the title screen once you have completed the game and seen any of the endings.

We're also adding support for the [i]SteelSeries keyboards[/i], where the keys will light up in different color depending on the current state of the game (menus, combats, enemy turn, etc) and also show all possible hotkeys for a quick visual cue of what they are.

There's also a fair amount of balance tweaks and bug fixes. Finally, there are a few changes to some data files and engines to be ready to support the upcoming DLC, although that's fully in the background for now. [b]The full patch notes are at the end of this post[/b]!


[h1]DLC News:[/h1]
We're still ironing out various DLC systems and we're not quite ready to reveal everything yet, but here's a very small subset of what the monster mini-classes are going to feel like in practice:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30514749/e6c1e7da0483fc2f1658c7dd90a60614ef7da2e4.png[/img]

There are a lot more options than this though, as we currently have over 15-20 different mini-classes in the works for monsters. Those classes aren't quite as big as human classes in terms of number of abilities, but each monster can currently equip two at once, which will provide a lot of options. We're still hammering out the details to make sure it's both fun and balanced though!


[h1]Follow us on Steam:[/h1]
A new system was added a little while ago to follow developers on Steams and be notified when they have new releases and such. If you want to make sure not to miss our upcoming DLC release, give it a try! You can follow us on Steam from our developer page, right here: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/6EyesStudio]6 Eyes Studio Steam Page[/url].


[h1]Change log:[/h1]
[u]10/11/2019 - Version 1.1.0[/u]
[h1]New Content:[/h1]
[list][*][b]New Game plus:[/b] Adding a New Game Plus option in the title screen. Upon clearing the game, the option will become available and the player can use the clear file to start a new game retaining various things from their previous game. The player can select what they retain and what is reset from a list of options.
[*][b]SteelSeries:[/b] Adding SteelSeries integration. When using a SteelSeries keyboard with per-key lighting capabilities, the keyboard will take different colors based on the current game state, and show all available hotkeys in white.
[*][b]New Male Portrait:[/b] Adding a forgotten male portrait.
[*][b]Optimizations:[/b] The game should load slightly faster than before.[/list]

[h1]Balance:[/h1]
[list][*][b]Healers:[/b] Updating the weights associated with healer classes to limit their count in maps where enemies are randomly generated. The net result should be less classes with healing spells in general.
[*][b]Bite:[/b] Increasing the base chance for the Poison effect to 62% (from 50%).
[*][b]Meatshield:[/b] Meatshield used to wear off when the target of it got its turn. Now it will wear off when the caster of it gets its turn (or it gets replaced by another Meatshield/cover effect). This will make it last longer and thus be more reliable/useful.
[*][b]New Recruits:[/b] When a class is unlocked, the player will always be able to switch to it, even if the requirements are not met. The main effect from this is when recruiting a unit in an advanced class (like Gambler for example), the unit will be able to switch back and forth to that class even if they don't meet the requirements.
[*][b]Missable Character:[/b] A certain character can't be recruited anymore after a certain point of the story has passed. There will now be a warning on the world map about the specific event vanishing soon if the player ignores it for too long.
[*][b]Double Cast:[/b] AI will be a little smarter with their second cast when using Double Cast. This is mostly a result of fixing a bug that make the second cast fizzle at times (it had other ramifications).
[*][b]Blood Suck:[/b] Increasing ratio bonus when the target is bleeding from 0.35x to 0.45x.
[*][b]Soul Suck:[/b] Increasing ratio bonus when the target is bleeding from 0.25x to 0.30x.
[*][b]Drain Health:[/b] Increasing damage ratio from 1x to 1.1x.
[*][b]Drain Soul:[/b] Increasing damage ratio from 0.35x to 0.45x.
[*][b]Gold Thread:[/b] Will now be granted as a victory reward in one of the late game story battles (this is not retroactive).
[*][b]Ancient Path:[/b] Small adjustments to a few random drop rates for ingredients.[/list]

[h1]UI:[/h1]
[list][*][b]Map Position:[/b] The map position will now update in the top left corner after an enemy has done moving.[/list]

[h1]Bugfixes:[/h1]
[list][*][b]Gelligh Treasures:[/b] If the player opened the treasures there "late into the story", it's possible it could have caused a problem with the "open all treasures" achievement. Fixed.
[*][b]Dialogues:[/b] Various small typos got fixed.
[*][b]Dash Strike/etc:[/b] Charge abilities would act weirdly when targeting large units. This is fixed.
[*][b]Class Change:[/b] The "Cancel sound" would play 2x in quick succession when leaving the screen. Fixed.
[*][b]Gogomboba City:[/b] Some extra units had their levels incorrectly set too high. Fixed.
[*][b]Maps:[/b] Fixing minor visuals issues with the grid on some maps.
[*][b]Vampire:[/b] Couldn't equip "cloth helmets" as they should. Fixed.
[*][b]Lists:[/b] Fixing a very rare case where a list would cause issues when empty and hitting confirm.
[*][b]Cleave:[/b] Fixing issues with Cleave not triggering at times: killing a target sporting Rebirth with a Collect ability, or with drowning wouldn't work correctly before.
[*][b]Screwworm Swamp:[/b] The map could be won by killing all allies. Fixed.
[*][b]Custom Portraits:[/b] Custom portraits had issues on Linux/Mac and would have issues if the user synced files across computers where the absolute customdata path was different. This is resolved. Save files will not save the absolute path of custom portraits anymore (that wasn't intended to begin with). Previous custom portraits shouldn't be affected, but if they are, setting them again at the guild should fix any issue.
[*][b]Enemy Passives:[/b] Fixing two instances of specific enemies having the same passive equipped twice.
[*][b]Pektites:[/b] Tier 3 red pektites had the wrong counter. Fixed.
[*][b]Meatshield:[/b] Fixing a rare crash with Meatshield.
[*][b]Sorting:[/b] Sorting units from the troops menu while in combat would have all sorts of weird issues. Disabling Sorting from the battle screen for now.
[*][b]Master of All:[/b] If a unit had mastered a class for which they didn't meet the requirements (so, a unit was recruited as an advanced class directly), that mastery wouldn't count towards the "Master of All" achievement. This should be fixed.
[*][b]Options:[/b] Selecting a line on the Options screen could feel unresponsive with the mouse as the far right side of the line wouldn't trigger the line selection without a click. Fixed.
[*][b]Arena:[/b] The enemies speed value wouldn't be used correctly on their first turn during arena matches (due to not being calculated until the match starts). Fixed. The turn-order might not be accurate until the match starts because of this.
[*][b]Pounce:[/b] It was possible for an enemy to use pounce to land on the same tile as another enemy that died with rebirth. Fixed.
[*][b]Dreadmaw:[/b] Ability was supposed to steal Buffs from the target, but that wasn't working correctly. Fixed.
[*][b]Dash Strike/etc:[/b] When an enemy would charge over a trap without having moved before, they would still be able to move after the trap interrupted the charge attack. Fixed.
[*][b]Dash Strike/etc:[/b] Under specific and rare circumstances, some the red tiles representing the charge area of effect could remain visible during targeting, even though they should have been erased.
[*][b]Descriptions:[/b] Fixing various descriptions typos.
[*][b]Loco Rush:[/b] Fixing a rare issue where a character might disappear oddly if there is no obvious valid destination when getting pushed around by Loco Rush.
[*][b]Spread Pain:[/b] Can now be used with Infused Edge and Focus Fire, as intended.
[*][b]Shoving Abilities:[/b] Fixing a wrong interaction between pushing abilities and targets with Mirage, where the Mirage would absorb the base damage but still displace the target or apply the bonus damage from the collision. Mirage now absorbs the whole effect.
[*][b]Music:[/b] Music could have a jump in volume when backing out on the Load menu from the Title screen. Fixed.
[*][b]Options:[/b] The Apply command in options list couldn't be clicked with the mouse before. Fixed.
[*][b]Double Cast:[/b] On rare occasions, when enemies would use Double Cast, their second spell could fizzle. Hopefully this is fixed now.
[*][b]Worms:[/b] Worms wouldn't use their breath attack as often as they should have due to a bug. Fixed.
[*][b]Kawa Bandits:[/b] Small adjustment to one of the early-game tables that had a typo, resulting in worse loot than it should have.
[*][b]Name Input:[/b] Using the "cancel key" in the name box would cancel the name input before. Fixed. Some minor mouse interactions were cleaned up as well.
[*][b]Obelisks:[/b] An extra check was added upon loading a save file to make sure the flag about having "all obelisks" is correctly set. There probably wasn't an issue on that side, but "just in case".
[*][b]Enemies:[/b] Once the player reached level 99, some enemies could be generated with story classes they shouldn't have access to. Fixed.[/list]

[h1]Modding:[/h1]
[list][*][b]Fonts:[/b] Adding a Vietnamese font to the list of available fonts for modders to use.
[*][b]Fonts:[/b] Adding a Japanese font to the list of available fonts for modders to use (it currently doesn't support Kanjis though).
[*][b]Errors:[/b] Adding more error checking for invalid data.
[*][b]Ingredients:[/b] Ingredients file will not require all sections to exist anymore (recipes, badges, gadgets, ingredients) and non-existent section will be treated as empty.
[*][b]Ingredients:[/b] Fixing some potential errors when modding this file where added data would behave oddly.
[*][b]Save Files:[/b] Slight update to the format to make it a little bit more efficient.[/list]

notes.title: A big thanks to everyone!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30514749/9f054c7bdc14380aa39bdaaf4d6d27a942f431ca.png[/img]

[h1]One year since our EA![/h1]
We launched our Steam Early Access on August 16th of 2018, so it's been about a year!

Looking at [I]Fell Seal[/I] today against what it was at the start of the Early Access really brings home the value of all the great feedback we received during that period (and afterwards as well)!

The balance improvements, various UI adjustments and AI upgrades that we've implemented during the EA were all greatly influenced by your comments and suggestions and it has made the game that much better for it!

[b]You guys are terrific and we couldn't have done it without your support![/b] So again, a big "[b]thank you[/b]" to everyone!


[h1]Nintendo Switch[/h1]
On another note, we released the [i]Nintendo Switch[/i] version of [i]Fell Seal[/i] a few days ago, which means it's now officially on all major consoles and all major PC platforms!

While it was quite the journey getting this far, we're still not quite done yet! And here's what's next...


[h1]What's coming next![/h1]
We've been working on a big DLC package for [i]Fell Seal[/i] for a while now, tentatively titled [b]Missions and Monsters[/b].

We're still wrapping up some of the core designs for it, but it should have a hefty amount of new things! 

It'll feature [b]recruitable monsters[/b] and  monsters "mini-classes"  which allow the player to customize their monster troops with quite a lot of options.

It'll have a new [b]missions system[/b] where the player can take on special quests from the Arbiter's Guild, expand the influence of the Arbiter's on various regions of the world and even upgrade the Guild with new buildings and features. There's a lot more to it, but we're still ironing out the intricacies of the system.

And of course, there will be new classes (including a monster-themed class), new encounters, new equipment, and a lot more! We'll also be releasing a new base update at some point before the DLC which will feature a [b]New Game+[/b] option, some QoL updates and more goodies. Stay tuned!

We want to keep everyone in the loop, so we're planning to have a Dev Log every few weeks during the creation of the DLC, just as soon as we start having some visuals to show for it!

And once again, thanks for all the support everyone!

notes.title: Build 1.0.4 - Bug fixes and small QoL updates
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30514749/4ffd165b042da04dfb469ce11b0850dd46f3d3bb.jpg[/img]
[h1]New Build[/h1]
Hello everyone!

We have a small update to the build today. For the most part it's bug fixes from what's been reported on the forums. Thanks to everyone that took the time to let us know about issues they've encountered!

We're also adding the option to exchange the confirm/cancel buttons on the gamepad, Switch button icons for the gamepad icons selection, some optimizations and a few balance tweaks tied to crafting components and Blood Magic. We're also adding a new difficulty option that will make the RNG "friendlier to the player" for those that would like that.

Finally, we updated the packaging for a few assets, which dropped the build size down by ~400MB.


[h1]Dreamhack[/h1]
We came back from Dreamhack a few days ago. Thanks to everyone that visited our booth!
The event was a lot of fun and the feedback great!

Thanks again!


[h1]Change log:[/h1]
[u]06/07/2019 - Version 1.0.4[/u]
[h1]UI:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Confirm/Cancel:[/b] Adding an option to invert the Confirm/Cancel buttons to the options.
[*][b]Loading Maps:[/b] Adding a "Loading..." text when a map is being loaded, to be clearer about it.
[*][b]Menus:[/b] Making menu navigation a little smoother, as some of the slower menus could have a bit of stutter on slower systems.
[*][b]Optimizations:[/b] Various small optimizations were made to reduce loading times.
[*][b]Build Size:[/b] Refactored a bunch of assets, which reduced the build size by about 500 MBs.
[*][b]Crafting:[/b] Kyrie reminds the player about crafting after a certain point in the story, but only if the player hasn't already visited the crafting screen. Now she will remind the player regardless.
[*][b]Holy Bolt:[/b] Renamed Ercinee "Holy Bolt" to "Sacred Bolt".
[*][b]Arena Prompt:[/b] Updating the arena prompt after winning a bout, to make it clear what the options are (Keep Fighting and Retire vs Yes and No).
[*][b]Gamepads:[/b] Adding the Switch icons to the list of Gamepad Icons so the player can select them. The Switch controller works in game but the player needs to set it to "Switch Gamepad Pro" in Steam beforehand and it won't use the Switch icons by default in game.
[/list]

[h1]Balance:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Difficulty:[/b] Changing the -15% to enemy stats difficulty option to -25% to enemy stats.
[*][b]Fetid Depths:[/b] Flagging some tiles as invalid destinations for displacement abilities, so the player can't be stuck on those tiles.
[*][b]Blood Magic:[/b] Changing conversion rate from 1.5% HP -> 1 MP to 2% HP -> 1 MP.
[*][b]Ending 2:[/b] Now showing a red node on the map when certain conditions are met, to show a specific node could be visited to get more information.
[*][b]Ancient Path:[/b] Now showing a red node when the Ancient Path initially opens, to help people notice it on the map. It's a secret dungeon though, so a little obfuscation is part of it.
[*][b]Distilled Water:[/b] Adding more drop locations for this crafting component in the last chapter of the story.
[*][b]Quality Thread:[/b] Adding slightly more drop locations for this crafting component.
[*][b]RNG:[/b] Adding a difficulty setting about Random numbers, with 2 options. The first option is the current system of rolling a simple d100 and using the result. The second option is "Skewed", which will skew the player's rolls in their favor a bit.
[*][b]Difficulty Settings:[/b] Changing the Easy preset to use the new "Player Friendly" random numbers system.
[/list]

[h1]Bugfixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Gamepads:[/b] When switching gamepads during play, it could happen that the help/options buttons would stop working on the new gamepad.
[*][b]Kawa Event:[/b] A specific event with some kawas could happen twice under specific circumstances. Fixed.
[*][b]Story Characters:[/b] Some story characters could have a weird Counter equipped when joining. Fixed.
[*][b]Typos:[/b] Fixing a few typos in the dialogues.
[*][b]Infernal Depth:[/b] Fixing a lava tile not flagged as lava correctly.
[*][b]Patrol Levels:[/b] Fixing a visual issue where the patrol level range could be shown to be over 99 (even though it would still be capped at 99 in practice).
[*][b]Manual Sorting:[/b] Manually sorting entries in the Troops menu would leave many characters walking in place. Fixed.
[*][b]Life Font:[/b] In some languages, the tooltip wasn't showing the correct information for that passive. Fixed.
[*][b]Vyscerawyrms:[/b] When spawning in a position with a unit, they could push the unit away in an invalid tile under rare circumstances. Fixed.
[*][b]Undies Set:[/b] Adding missing frames to this outfit.
[*][b]Changing Appearance:[/b] Going into the "Change Appearance" menu at the guild after dismissing all possible units would crash the game. Fixed.
[*][b]Patented Usage:[/b] When the AI used an item through Patented Usage, it would not decrease the amount of item uses left for the item in question. Fixed.
[*][b]Turn Order:[/b] The turn order bar wouldn't update correctly (until their next turn) when removing Haste or Slow from a unit. Fixed.
[*][b]Pushing Attacks:[/b] There was a rare case where the AI could use a push ability on a target that's immune to displacements, thinking it would be useful. Fixed.
[*][b]AI Weapons:[/b] There was a very rare case where an enemy could have a Bow/Crossbow in their main hand and a gun in their offhand. Fixed.
[*][b]Grandhalls:[/b] During battle dialogues, a certain character could look towards the wrong direction while talking to another character. Fixed.
[*][b]Chilling Touch:[/b] Chilling Touch and similar passives would list a % chance in the prediction box for Sabotage and Teleport Other, even though it won't work. Fixed.
[/list]

notes.title: Build 1.0.3 is live! - Bug fixes, QoL, balance updates
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30514749/8114835af08f6bf165b3a2f5e4c3c92c033b1436.jpg[/img]
[h1]Build 1.0.3[/h1]
Hello everyone!

We're pushing another update today focusing mainly on [b]fixing all the bugs[/b] that have been found since release, as well as some [b]QoL changes[/b], especially centered around mouse usage. We also have a [b]few balance tweaks[/b], although that wasn't the focus of this patch.

Here are some of the more noticeable changes:
[list]
[*][b]Balance:[/b] Various small changes to make the enemies take less advantage of "drowning" the player.
[*][b]Mouse:[/b] While in the troops menu, the mouse will allow the user to select a new character by clicking on them, even if they aren't in the "select character" phase (mouse over a unit on the camp screen, click the left button to select them).
[*][b]Mouse Movement:[/b] Reducing the frequency at which the "cursor moved" sound can play on the battle map when moving the battle cursor with the mouse.
[*][b]Show Details:[/b] Can now be used by pressing-and-holding the mouse cursor over the bottom right hint.
[*][b]Self Targetting:[/b] Will now skip the "select unit" phase and directly select the caster to save a superfluous step.
[*][b]Movements:[/b] When in battle, clicking on the map will act as if "move" had been clicked, which should reduce mouse movement on the screen when trying to move a unit with the mouse.
[*][b]Injuries:[/b] Regular injuries (not permanent injuries) will now show the units 4 stats in red in the menu, unless they have passives that increase those stats.
[/list]

The full list of changes is at the end of this post.


[h1]Shout out![/h1]
We also wanted to give a shout-out to our good friends at Overhype Studios about their newest DLC, [i]Battle Brothers - Warriors of the North[/i], which was released yesterday.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30514749/f6874e8de0c31042e3d0300f914158cb6ee6e199.png[/img]

If you haven't checked out [i]Battle Brothers[/i] yet, you should give it a look right here: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/365360/Battle_Brothers/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/365360/Battle_Brothers/[/url]


[h1]Change log:[/h1]
[u]05/10/2019 - Version 1.0.3[/u]
[h1]UI:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Mouse:[/b] While in the troops menu, the mouse will allow the user to select a new character by clicking on them, even if they aren't in the "select character" phase (mouse over a unit on the camp screen, click the left button to select them).
[*][b]Mouse Movement:[/b] Reducing the frequency at which the "cursor moved" sound can play on the battle map when moving the battle cursor with the mouse.
[*][b]Show Details:[/b] Can now be used by pressing-and-holding the mouse cursor over the bottom right hint.
[*][b]Self Targetting:[/b] Will now skip the "select unit" phase and directly select the caster to save a superfluous step.
[*][b]Movements:[/b] When in battle, clicking on the map will act as if "move" had been clicked, which should reduce mouse movement on the screen when trying to move a unit with the mouse.
[*][b]Status Effects in Combat:[/b] Increasing the maximum amount of status effects listed in the "damage phase" from 6 to 8.
[*][b]Steal Gold:[/b] Gold value was shown with very small text before. Fixed.
[*][b]Injuries:[/b] Regular injuries (not permanent injuries) will now show the units 4 stats in red in the menu, unless they have passives that increase those stats.
[*][b]Performance:[/b] Minor performance improvements.
[*][b]Spearvault:[/b] Will now look better when casted from under-water.
[/list]

[h1]Balance:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Drowning:[/b] Adding a 33% chance that an enemy will ignore "drowning/lava dunking" targets on their turn even if it's the best move they can do.
[*][b]Ekidna Falls:[/b] Rakkerjaks on this map will no longer be upgraded to tier2 if the player is high enough level.
[*][b]Highlands:[/b] Making some changes to the elite version of the encounter to prevent a scenario where the elite enemy would Snapback on the guests too early and lead to a near unavoidable defeat.
[*][b]Achievements:[/b] The achievement about mastering all the classes on a certain special character will now not count their "secret end-game class" as being needed.
[*][b]Timber Roads:[/b] Reducing the levels of a few units in the Patrols, to make them a little bit easier.
[*][b]Beginner Maps:[/b] Beginner maps with a very low max level for enemies, made to help the player level up beginner units, will now yield less AP/GP than normal if the player's highest level units are higher than that zone.
[*][b]Skyjack:[/b] Will now not move people to locations that are off-limits for teleport-other (such as very high ledges, etc).
[*][b]Azure Plains:[/b] Moving one of the Vangals to the Elite difficulty to make the map easier.
[*][b]Maps:[/b] For Gelligh, marking some of the tiles as invalid destinations for "teleport-other" to reduce chances of characters getting stranded where they shouldn't.
[*][b]Meteorites:[/b] Adding a meterorite drop to 1 story encounter and 1 optional encounter. Also as a random drop to some late maps.
[*][b]Leap:[/b] Counters will now consider leap's destination (rather than starting point), which means it behaves like an "adjacent attack" for the targets.
[*][b]Final Battle:[/b] Updating the 2 ending battle maps to have better drops in general. The Ancient Path is still a better spot overall to get rare drops, but these 2 maps should feel more rewarding now.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Displacements:[/b] Fixing an issue where enemies immune to being displaced could still be displaced by Pandora's Box or Skyjack.
[*][b]Mount Nervanzer:[/b] Fixing an issue with a character showing over a tile while jumping.
[*][b]Claret Woods:[/b] Fixing an issue with an enemy spawning on a spot they can't escape from.
[*][b]Try and Buy:[/b] Purchase couldn't go through if the cost and player gold were the same. Fixed.
[*][b]Title Screen:[/b] Fixing a rare issue with timing for users with an invalid time zone setting on their OS (still not sure how that's even possible, haha).
[*][b]UI:[/b] Fixing various non-fatal errors tied to rare edge cases when navigating the UI. It probably won't have a noticeable impact on most users, but if something behaved oddly once in a while, it'll be probably be fixed.
[*][b]Bootup:[/b] Fixing a potential error when starting the game for users that might have deleted folders they shouldn't have in "My Documents\Fell Seal".
[*][b]Turkish Locale:[/b] Fixing some potential issues with the titlescreen on Turkish locale.
[*][b]Dreadmaw:[/b] If there were status effects applied by the attack, their text would remain on the screen at the end of the attack. Fixed.
[*][b]Maps:[/b] Fixing some drawing ordering issues for some maps.
[*][b]Archafflictor:[/b] The Bzil variant had 3 jump instead of 4. Fixed.
[*][b]Title Screen:[/b] Under specific circumstances, the titlescreen animated image could be shown too zoomed-out/in. This should be fixed.
[*][b]The Gauntlet:[/b] When certain special enemies would die, some of the map tiles would become "walkable", even though they shouldn't have.
[*][b]Thespeiros:[/b] An NPC walking around town could sometimes start walking in places he shouldn't. Fixed.
[*][b]Wild Cards:[/b] The case where Wild Card has a critical miss and applies the opposite effect will now not result in a 'miss' unless the target is immune to the effect (ie, it will refresh the duration if the target has it).
[*][b]Chitin Armor:[/b] A certain treasure was granting the wrong armor (Dendrite Armor) instead of the Chitin Armor. This is fixed, but is not retroactive unfortunately.
[*][b]Bzil Classes:[/b] When learning a Bzil class, there was a chance the popup would remain visible if there was a cutscene happening after the battle. There were other instances where this could happen with popups at the end of combat. All fixed.
[*][b]Descriptions:[/b] Fixing some typos and mistakes in some descriptions.
[*][b]Spell Effects:[/b] After using Plaguestorm or Hippocampos, subsequent spells might be partially misplaced on screen. Fixed.
[/list]


[u]05/12/2019 - Version 1.0.3a[/u]
[h1]Bugfixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Doublecast:[/b] Will not be useable after using a contextual command (like gather, open, climb, etc), unless the passive to that effect is equipped.
[*][b]Mods:[/b] Badge names will not become invisible anymore when using a custom crafting file.
[*][b]Help Compendium:[/b] Adaptive affinity was misnamed in the help description about buffs. Fixed.
[/list]

notes.title: Fell Seal: Arbiter's Mark finally, fantastically and tactically exits early acccess
notes.notes:
Fell Seal: Arbiter’s Mark may not be the greatest strategy RPG in the world (I’ve not played enough make that call), but developers 6 Eyes Studio have produced a fine tribute. Leaving early access today after an active year of tweaking, tuning and adding new missions, it’s a strategy RPG in the style of Final Fantasy Tactics, probably my favourite game in its genre. That means turn-based high-fantasy stabbery, looting and levelling, with a heavy focus on positioning, complex terrain and even more complex character builds. See the launch trailer below, or snag a demo here.

notes.title: Friday Progress Report!
notes.notes:
[h1]Progress Report[/h1]
It is finally done! [I]Fell Seal: Arbiter's Mark[/I] is complete and releasing in a few days (April 30th)!
 
It's been an intense adventure and while it's been a lot of fun, it's also been a lot of hard work. We finally made it to the finish line and now all that's left is to wait for the reaction of the fans :)
 
We think our Early Access has gone quite well and if we could "do it all over again", we'd definitely still chose to go with an Early Access. It has been invaluable in helping us balance the game better and helping us refine the UI and systems even better.
 
An immense [b]thank you[/b] to everyone that's taken the time to give us their feedback!
You guys are the best!
 

[h1]What's next[/h1]
We're not sure what's the next move for us. We'll definitely make another game after this one, but is it going to be Fell Seal DLC, Fell Seal 2 or a completely different game? We'll have to wait and see.
At this point, if the fans are interested in Fell Seal DLC, it's probably our first option. If not, we'll probably move on to another project altogether rather than Fell Seal 2. We'll consider a second entry in the saga for a later game though, that's for sure!
 
We'll also be supporting [i]Fell Seal[/i] for as long as necessary, fixing any bugs we might have missed before release and keeping an eye on how the balance of the game is looking and if we need to address anything. We also have list of upgrades we'd like to get in and we'll probably start looking at those in a few weeks (after a small vacation most likely. It's been so long we took one of those >.<)

Which means we won't be pushing an update every Friday anymore, unless it's somehow needed, but that would be quite surprising!


Once again, [b]a big thank you to the whole community [/b]from the two of us here at 6 Eyes Studio! :)

notes.title: Build 0.9.5c
notes.notes:
Yet another small update! ^^

We're making a build for another platform today, so we thought we'd push the same changes on Steam for parity. It's mostly bug fixes and tiny ui/balance tweaks.

[b]We're not planning anymore updates until Release [/b]at this point, although the Release build will have some more bug fixes and UI tweaks.

Here's the change log:
[u]04/22/2019 - Version 0.9.5c[/u]
[h1]Bug Fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Trapdoors:[/b] Trapdoors stopped working with the new Turn order changes. Fixed.
[*][b]Placement:[/b] Selecting enemies during placement would sometimes highlight the wrong portrait in the Turn order bar.
